title: Too Old to Have a Baby?

blanks.section: NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS — Changing patterns of parenthood

blanks.sentence: Two factors linked to later motherhood are better access to _____.
Having a baby later in life may also involve _____.
In many countries, women now have their first baby when they are _____.
A former label for mothers over 35 was considered _____ by many people.
Compared with women, men may remain _____ for longer.
Some young women in the West say they intend to have _____.

multipleChoice.question: What change does the researcher describe across recent decades?
options: First births have shifted from women's thirties to much younger ages.
Having a first child after 30 has become common in many countries.
Women in every country now begin motherhood after turning 30.
First births have become less frequent only among women in their thirties.

multipleChoice.question: What distinction does the presenter make between the former label for mothers over 35 and social attitudes?
options: It was replaced because most mothers now start having children before 35.
It remains in common use although social attitudes have become more positive.
Its meaning changed when women started having children in their thirties.
Its use has ended, while negative attitudes towards older mothers can remain.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the older male celebrity's later child mentioned?
options: To illustrate men's ability to father children beyond women's usual fertile years.
To show that older fathers usually have more children than younger fathers do.
To explain why women's natural fertility begins to decline during their forties.
To suggest that becoming a father later is common among male celebrities.

multipleChoice.question: According to the researcher, what may contribute to praise for an older father?
options: People may admire his willingness to raise a child without a partner.
People may assume he has chosen to delay his career for parenthood.
People may notice that he has a considerably younger partner.
People may believe he has avoided the health risks of later parenthood.

multipleChoice.question: How do the reactions in the researcher's comparison differ?
options: Both parents tend to receive praise, but the father receives it more publicly.
The older father may be congratulated, while the older mother may cause discomfort.
The older father may cause concern, while the older mother may be congratulated.
Both parents may make people uncomfortable, though for different reasons.

multipleChoice.question: What is the researcher's attitude to the difference in reactions?
options: She regards it as an expected result of medical differences.
She thinks it is mainly a question of the parents' exact ages.
She treats it as a reaction limited to famous parents.
She presents it as a problem involving gender.

multipleChoice.question: What can be concluded from the final comparison of young women in the West and women in more traditional countries?
options: Views about having children can differ substantially between social settings.
Young women in both settings are increasingly refusing motherhood.
Women in traditional settings generally become mothers at younger ages.
Western women tend to want children only after establishing careers.
